title: Ordered Bayer dither pass to levels or a palette
purpose: Dither a three.js frame with a 2, 4, 8 or 16 wide Bayer matrix to a fixed number of levels per channel or to the nearest of up to 16 palette colours, in pixel blocks and in sRGB-encoded or linear values, as a ShaderPass definition or full-screen ShaderMaterial with an exact CPU mirror of every output pixel.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE (integer bit operations of GLSL ES 3.00, int uniforms, a vec3 array uniform and the colorspace_fragment chunk); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

exports.name: createOrderedDitherShader
exports.summary: A fresh shader definition for three.js ShaderPass or ShaderMaterial; the palette is a flat array of 16 colours.

exports.name: createOrderedDitherMaterial
exports.summary: The definition as a full-screen ShaderMaterial without depth test or write.

exports.name: bayerMatrix
exports.summary: The n x n Bayer matrix (n = 2, 4, 8, 16) built recursively.

exports.name: bayerThreshold
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the shader threshold (M + 0.5) / n^2, computed bit by bit.

exports.name: ditherSamplePixel
exports.summary: The pixel whose input colour a block reads.

exports.name: ditherPixel
exports.signature: ditherPixel(rgb, x, y, options = {}) -> [r, g, b]
exports.summary: CPU mirror of one output pixel.

exports.name: ORDERED_DITHER_FRAGMENT
exports.summary: Fragment stage: block sample, threshold, levels or palette.

options.name: matrixSize
options.meaning: Bayer matrix width; larger gives finer gradients.

options.name: mode
options.meaning: Quantize each channel to levels, or pick the nearest palette colour.

options.name: levels
options.meaning: Levels per channel in levels mode.

options.name: palette
options.meaning: 1 to 16 colours in the dithering domain (sRGB-encoded values in the srgb domain).

options.name: spread
options.meaning: Palette mode: how far the threshold moves the colour before the nearest-colour search.

options.name: pixelSize
options.meaning: Block size in output pixels; each block reads one input pixel and one threshold.

options.name: domain
options.meaning: Dither sRGB-encoded values (even perceptual steps) or the linear values received.

options.name: resolution
options.meaning: Output size in pixels; update uResolution on resize.

limits: Ordered dithering only: no error diffusion, blue noise or temporal dithering, so the cross-hatch of the Bayer matrix shows. The palette search is a nearest colour by Euclidean distance in the dithering domain, not a perceptual colour difference, and ties keep the earlier colour. The pattern is tied to output pixels (gl_FragCoord), so it stays fixed on screen while the image moves. uResolution must match the output size, or blocks read the wrong input pixel. HDR inputs are clamped to [0, 1]. Output goes through three.js's output colour space conversion. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Bayer ordered dither matrix by the recursion M(2n) = [[4M, 4M + 2], [4M + 3, 4M + 1]]
Bit-interleaved threshold computation from the most significant bit
Threshold-offset rounding to levels and nearest-palette search
